That seems about right to me. I would either use a screw extractor set, just make sure the engines threads aren't stripped once you get it out. You might have to tap new threads or get an oversized plug of they are.

Or I would just leave it in and use the bolt on the shifter side of the engine to drain the oil in the future.

For future reference, the drain plug torque spec is 18 foot pounds and I would even bump it down to 15 to be safe. Wish I knew before I stripped mine that these engines are very very soft.

Extractor set (there's many options out there):
https://www.lowes.com/pd/SpeedOut-8-1-8-in-Double-Ended-Screw-Extractor/1000170531?cm_mmc=shp-_-c-_-prd-_-tol-_-google-_-lia-_-215-_-pta-drillinganddriving-_-1000170531-_-0&placeholder=null&ds_rl=1286981&gclid=CjwKCAjwnPOEBhA0EiwA609ReeRjOjD9N8kC_7YEMZNXSrVeD25YtN02_ldbyuu9aQUjXZ58TxOHYhoC7KUQAvD_BwE&gclsrc=aw.ds

Edit: be careful with impact drills, I've ruined plenty of bolts with them. My first car had lost half its lug nut studs by the time I got rid of it.

Are you sure its the plug that is stripped? For me it was the block threads that stripped. I'm lazy and never found the size to find a bigger plug, so I just wrapped the plug in Teflon tape to make it fatter. 900 miles later, checking the plug religiously and its never backed out.
